quoted.text:
Lamar Jackson says he watched friends chase fast money while he was playing the long game and counting how many years it would take him to reach the NFL

“I’m seeing my friends who I was growing up with who I was playing football with… Just throw their life away for fast money and stuff like that. They used to tell me ‘Oh, you talk too much’. Because I used to always speak about football and positivity stuff. They didn’t want to hear that.”

“Now it’s like… They’d rather hear it now because I’m Lamar Jackson. But I’ve been speaking about it. Everybody just wasn’t listening. I was already seeing what was going on. I wish we could go back in time and y’all could see what I was seeing. Because I always looked at life like, I counted years.”

“Like I would think… ‘How many years does it take to get to the league?’ They’re saying… ‘You do three years in college.’ I said… ‘I’m doing three years.’ I’m not doing four. I’m not trying to go fifth year. I’m doing three years because I’m going to make sure my family is good.”

“If you’re coming from a place like where I come from, don’t try to be like the guys around you. Don’t look up to the stuff that looks like it’s fun… Because sometimes it gets you in trouble.”

“It’s sacrificing. ‘Man, I can’t have fun right now. I’ve got to get my family right. I can’t do this right now. I can’t mess up.’ Forget the fast money. I’ve got to think about longevity.”

“You can get locked up and do five years for $1,000. That money gone. It’s gone. You’re like… ‘Man, I just did that for $1,000…’ And I could have waited five years and I would’ve had $10 million.”

“That’s why I’m where I’m at right now. That’s how I used to think. My mom working… She’s busting her behind. It’s me, my brother and my two sisters at home. I’m the oldest…”

“So I’ve got to make sure everybody right. And it’s like… Man, I can’t wait, but I’ve got to wait. That’s the sacrifice. I’ve got to be patient. People don’t look at it like that. It’s like… ‘Man, I need that money right now.’ But you don’t need that money right now. Just wait.”

items.text: *Chefs kiss* https://t.co/t8hW83rT9A

This probably shouldn't bother me, but it just does whenever I see Friday Night Lights.

In the first 45 seconds of this clip, Permian stops the Dallas team on 4th and inches.  Simultaneously, both coaches make about as bad a play decision as is possible.  Let's review:

Billy Bob Thornton's character calls a "Texas Twist" and describes a stunt game intended to get their superstar end through the A gap, which is simply going to take far too long to develop for any chance at a stop.

However, his lollipop-sucking adversary from Dallas calls a ridiculously slow-developing run play (it almost looks like a draw based on the depth of the handoff), which was just the proper amount of stupid to let Permian get in the backfield.

I'm guessing there are a lot of Texas high-school football fans who are/were equally perturbed by this play calling.

Great movie, bad football.
